reviews.author: Andrea Shaw
reviews.text:
One of the worst things that can happen (at least to me) is getting sick or having an emergency when I’m away from home. I’m from New Jersey and found myself in Florida with a sudden dental emergency. The kind of pain that keeps you up all night. I didn’t get a single wink of sleep. In the early hours of the morning, desperate and exhausted, I found this dental group online and was sitting in their office by 8:30am.

From the moment I walked in, they took incredible care of me. The front desk team was so kind and welcoming, which immediately put me at ease. The dental assistant was patient and comforting, and the dentist himself Dr. Perras was beyond amazing, so gentle, attentive, and reassuring throughout the entire visit. I have a very low tolerance for pain, and I can honestly say I did not feel any pain at all. That has NEVER been my experience at a dentist before.

In fact m, and this is wild,  I actually fell asleep while they were actively working on me. Who falls asleep during a dental procedure?! That has to mean something. I came in running on zero sleep from being up all night in pain, and somehow I was relaxed enough in that chair to knock out. That alone speaks volumes about how gentle and skilled they are.

On top of the exceptional care, the pricing was more than fair. I was fully expecting astronomical emergency pricing for an appointment I had booked barely an hour earlier  but that wasn’t the case at all.

And to top it off, they called me the very next morning to check on me and see how I was feeling. That level of follow-up and genuine care is rare.

I can’t recommend this office enough. If relocating to Florida just to have this dentist permanently was practical… I’d honestly consider it. 😂

Thank you for turning such a stressful, painful situation into such a positive experience.

reviews.text:
A-pril 2025 -  While vacationing in Florida, due to an unfortunate and terrible mishap,  I incurred blunt force trauma to my head, face and teeth.  Upon release from the hospital's ER, I was handed a list of Dental Emergency Trauma Clinics with strict instructions from the ER doctor to contact one immediately. Much to my demise it was just after office hours and many where closed. However I did manage to reach one clinic. I explained the situation as best as I could although having trouble verbalizing.  They offered to have the doctor paged and I was to await his call.  Immediately after hanging up, an emergency alert came across my phone... there was an active shooting taking place at Florida State University. Oh no not again I thought to myself.  While waiting for the doctor to call, I felt a need to pray for the safety of the poor people trapped inside that university and the terror they must be experiencing.  After a little while my phone rang.  It was Dr. Slaybaugh from DWIC of Tampa Bay and he agreed to see me.  I was so afraid of what the x-rays would reveal.  With kindness and compassion he explained to me exactly what needed to be done. So with Dr. Slaybaugh's reassurance I decided to place my fate into his hands and I'm glad I did.  I have front teeth again and they look even better than they did before.  In fact I even smile more now.  Thank you Dr. Slaybaugh for giving my self confidence a boost.  You don't know what that means to me.  I came in with teeth in my hand looking like I'd been in a train wreck and walked out looking like a swan. DWIC of Tampa you will always be number one in my book.  Everyone there makes you feel like family. High praises for all of you.

Now I need to mention something really special. I know your probably all wondering why I mentioned the Florida State University shooting. Well I didn't find this out until much later but the day and time of that shooting was the exact time I was waiting for a return call from the doctor which DWIC had paged and told me to await his call. It's clear to me now why I felt the need to pray for the people trapped in the university at that time. It just so happens that Dr. Slaybaugh has a family member who attends Florida State University, and was present there at the time of the shooting. Fortunately the family member was unharmed.

reviews.author: Teshon Thomas
reviews.text:
I chose Jackson Dental because of their strong reviews and initially had confidence in the office and Dr. Fortier. I came in specifically to replace two crowns because the shade of my older crowns no longer matched my natural teeth after whitening over time. I was assured a proper shade match could be achieved.

Unfortunately, when the new crowns were placed, they appeared noticeably too white compared to my surrounding teeth. I voiced concerns immediately, and it was obvious I wasn’t satisfied even after the in-office adjustments the doctor made. Dr. Fortier encouraged me to “give it two weeks” and said if I still wasn’t satisfied, they would work with me to fix it. Based on those conversations, I believed adjustments could be made if needed and moved forward with cementing them.

After trying to make it work  including spending over $400 on professional whitening and additional whitening products to try to match my natural teeth to the crowns  I remained unhappy with the result.

My biggest concern is this: At no point during the planning, shade matching, or crown fabrication process was I told there were different crown material options that might affect esthetics, nor was I told that if the result was unsatisfactory, correcting it later could involve an additional $500–$1,000. That was never part of the conversation. I was simply given confidence that they “had it,” and the crowns were made. Only after I expressed dissatisfaction did I hear about alternate materials, lighting issues during shade matching, and significant remake costs!

That is what felt unacceptable. Information that important should be discussed before treatment is finalized, not introduced only after a patient is unhappy and being asked to pay a substantial sum again. If material choices could have impacted the result, that should have been presented upfront so I could make an informed decision. Shifting that burden to the patient afterward did not feel fair or professional.

What frustrated me most was not just the aesthetic result, but the lack of transparency and follow-through. To be fair, someone from the front desk did call me back and offered whitening, but I had already spent over $400 doing that, so that did not address the actual concern. I was told they would do more digging and get back to me. I later followed up again myself, left a voicemail requesting to speak with someone because I was unhappy with the visit, and weeks later I have still not heard back from management or anyone in charge. That made me feel dismissed.

I’m not questioning anyone’s intentions, but as a patient spending significant money on cosmetic dental work, I expected informed discussion of options, transparency about potential costs, and meaningful support when concerns were raised. I hope this feedback helps improve the patient experience going forward.

reviews.author: Carley Carter
reviews.text:
BEWARE OF OVERCHARGING!

I strongly recommend that any patient here carefully compare every charge to their insurance EOB. Do not assume the billing is accurate without verifying it yourself!

After personally reconciling the office's patient ledger to my insurance Explanation of Benefits, I found over $5k in billing discrepancies. Line by line, I found charges that exceeded the insurance-allowed amounts. For example, one visit was billed at $467, while the allowed amount was $251. These differences were not minor—they added up to a substantial overpayment!
What’s troubling is that these discrepancies were not identified or corrected by the office. I had to do the reconciliation myself and bring it to their attention.

After submitting detailed documentation, including a very detailed and thorough spreadsheet, persistent follow ups and ultimately escalated to take legal action until I finally received a partial refund, well beyond the expected timeframe. Even now, the amount is not fully resolved, and $252 remains in dispute.

When billing discrepancies of this size only come to light after a patient conducts their own detailed audit—and then require weeks of pressure to partially correct—it raises serious questions about billing accuracy and internal oversight.

Also want to note that they require full payment for procedures up front and don't take in account estimated insurance proceeds. As a result, I ended up over paying by more than $10k! What makes this whole situation worse is that I used to really like this office, had a lot of trust and respect for them but the way I've been treated ever since I started questioning the charges has done a complete 180. They consistently made me feel like a burden and the "bad guy". They did not take accountability at all for the issue and continue to argue with me with no substantial back up.

Regarding the actual dental work I received - when I went in to switch out my temporary crowns to the permanent ones (I got crowns on almost all my top teeth), I really didn't like them and weren't like the temporary ones I was wearing for a few weeks. I was almost in tears trying to advocate for myself before they permanently cemented them. They made me feel bad for sending them back, I'm so glad I got the courage to speak up and not accept something I did not like. Ultimately after the second visit, they ended up looking really good but after everything I've dealt with recently, I certainly won't be returning. Who knows how much they overcharged me since 2019 when I first started coming here!

If you chose to go to this office, please make sure to pay close attention to your patient charges and the amount they submit to your dental insurance (they should match)! If they owe you a refund, Florida recently based a law that makes it unlawful for healthcare providers to hold onto amounts owed to patients for overpayments over 30 days.

reviews.author: Emily
reviews.text:
I had been a cavity-free, no-issue dental patient my entire life before coming here. Jackson Dental suddenly told me I had “pre-gum disease,” with pocket readings of 4s and 5s — numbers I’d never heard in my life. They pushed expensive deep cleanings, three visits a year instead of two, antibiotic packing in my gums, fluoride treatments I had to pay out-of-pocket despite having great insurance, and constantly tried to upsell me on retainers and cosmetic procedures. I was genuinely alarmed.
I got a second opinion, then eventually switched dentists entirely — without mentioning any of this. The new hygienist told me unprompted that there was “no plaque to even pick off” my teeth, my gum readings were all 1s and 3s, and she actually paused to comment on how healthy my gums were and that they didn’t even bleed.
This place either has a serious quality problem or is deliberately upselling healthy patients. Either way, get a second opinion before agreeing to anything here.​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​ Also they’re friendly because they get commission if you mention their name in a review.

I recommend Jackson Dental to everyone.

reviews.author: Jennifer Johnson
reviews.text:
Shared at patients request.   Aun Ali recommends Smile Design Dentistry (Downtown Tampa).
August 8 ·
Hello,
I would like to write a thoughtful review on my experience  with hygienist ,Jennifer Johnson   I will be switching to this office but saw her in a different office a couple years ago   I want to share my review as  Jen is someone I highly recommend without reservation. I, for one, am hesitant when going to a dentist's office to begin with. She was on point in several factors. Her smile and a welcoming greeting set the stage for what I knew would be an excellent experience. She sat me down and made sure I was comfortable and relaxed as I can possibly be. Starting out, she thoroughly went over my X-rays and informed me on the status of practically every tooth. While filling out paperwork, she had me sit back and watch a very informative video on gum anatomy. She took her time from start to finish. I wanted to rush out and start my day but she didn't want that lol. My gums where inflamed for months and I just lived with it. Jennifer kept reassuring me on how good I would feel in the days to come. To be honest, I underestimated that. She was so precise to make sure every tooth is 100 percent and I know that because instead of hurrying up and finishing my whole mouth, she only did half and said " I want to do a good job and I need two sessions for this." Wasn't the best news given my busy schedule. I said sure. I felt the effect, the very next day as the inflammation around my molar was beginning to subside. I came back much more happily the second time for the rest of my mouth excited to see what the overall results would be. The best part about this whole experience was how pain free it really was. In the beginning, I felt only a mild discomfort and without even telling her, she numbed me up more. I can easily tell she wants her patients to be completely pain free. Couple weeks have past by and I have forgotten the pain I was living in and thank God for introducing me to Jennifer. I say this again, I highly recommend her without reservation.
Aun Hussain MD
Vascular and Interventional Radiology

I was also told that they take my insurance, only to have the whole visit cost over $1,700. I was not offered any anesthetic besides numbing shots and laughing gas even though anesthesia is listed on the website and on the forms they had me fill out and I let them know ahead of time how anxious I was. When I called to confirm before I went in I was told I would be given pain meds and antibiotics. I was given neither and my tongue and throat were numb so I could not ask about them, and I could not even take ibuprofen until the numbing shot wore off. I was definitely taken advantage of. None of the services I had done were worth $1,700- especially not being put under anesthesia and not given any medications to go home with or any stitches. The only thing they did were x-rays and then they numbed me and took my teeth out and sent me on my way (after waiting 3 hours in the waiting room). I felt like I was in a chop shop. I was scared of dentists before, but now I am absolutely petrified.

reviews.author: Pixel Doctor
reviews.text:
Do not go here. Classic case of a chain dentist company trying to get as much money off you as possible.

For starters I am a younger guy and take excellent care of my teeth. I brush and floss twice a day with a timed electric tooth brush and use a non-whitening, enamel repairing toothpaste. I understand even with taking perfect care of your teeth that you can still need work done based on so many other factors(genetics, diet, etc.). The only thing I went here for was a cleaning since it had been some time since my last one. There was absolutely nothing I noticed wrong with my teeth. When I first arrived, I waited 30 minutes in the chair for someone to start working with me. Secondly, I was told by the dentist that she could tell based off my x-rays that I grind my teeth. I most certainly DO NOT grind my teeth in any way, I want to reinstate that I am a younger guy and am surprised of the tone she used when saying this as she made me out to sound like an old man who has been grinding his teeth his whole life. She used this to say I needed a dental night guard that was $120 dollars! You can buy one at Walmart for $20. She also absolutely forced this onto me and didn’t even ask me if I wanted it. She just put it on my bill and it wasn’t until I was speaking to a different person that I said I didn’t want that. To make a bad situation worse, I was so nonchalantly told that I needed to get a filling redone, because it was worn down. The manner in which this was expressed to me was as if it was no big deal. Not like I’m getting a syringe put in my mouth and injected with a numbing substance and getting my teeth worn down🙂. The biggest surprise is that my teeth feel completely fine, I have no bad sensation in my teeth and don’t feel any sort of pain or cavity related feelings. Obviously given the fact I have a filling I know what a cavity feels like and I don’t feel that at all. I’ve heard horror stories of people getting fillings redone when they aren’t needed. I wasn’t going to be another one of those…

My recommendation, stay away from corporate chains and go to a private practice where the name of the place is the dentist who is doing the work…

I went in to Tampa Dentistry for a basic/routine teeth cleaning. My dental insurance covers 2 cleanings for free including X-rays (1x per year) which is excellent. The dentistry still charged me at the door anyways when they shouldn’t have but I paid anyways. I think for a required “Tooth Inspection” where they tell you your teeth look great before cleaning them.

The staff was nice & friendly but it was clear they spent next to no money on equipment or supplies compared to other dentistries. The cleaning mainly consisted of a metal toothpick, a toothbrush, and some dental floss. While the staff seem competent, the supplies looked as low-grade as it gets.

I already wasn’t planning on going back based on that alone but the trigger for this review was the weirdness of getting emails and text messages for a new dental bill!

I had declined the fluoride upcharge and already paid at the door which alone was an incorrect/double billing since my dental insurance makes it all free. I have never had a dental bill message before in my 20+ years of experience of basic teeth cleanings roughly twice per year. In that experience, the only times I’ve had to pay at the door (with dental insurance) was if I accepted the fluoride up-charge. Super shady. It’s worth the drive to go somewhere else.

reviews.text: Have been going to this dental practice for 8 years. It has always been a pleasant experience!  The employees are just the best!  Welcoming and pleasant!  I look forward to my appointments!! And to seeing my new dentist!!

reviews.author: Kristin Crawford
reviews.text: I have been going to this office for 25 years. They are the best. I had a loose cap that Dr. Christina recemented for me.  She is excellent.

reviews.author: Gregory A. Kaalund
reviews.text: Great cleaning experience! Polite, nice and very professional!

reviews.author: Franci Neuge
reviews.text: Love the staff at Tampa Dental: Front desk are always pleasant and patient; Dr. Nick, Dr Christina, Hygienists Kathy & Stephanie are gentle, friendly and very thorough. My whole family are patients and I have referred others.

reviews.author: Rebecca Parrott
reviews.text: Quick, on-time and done. perfect crown!!

reviews.author: Joe
reviews.text: Excellent experience all around. Everyone was polite, professional, and very friendly. Dr. Villafria and Kelsi were phenomenal and made the dreaded dentist visit into an enjoyable one. Look forward to coming back here for sure.

reviews.author: Charles Klass
reviews.text: Excellent service by a professional, caring, courteous, and friendly dentist and staff.

reviews.author: Shelley Lee
reviews.text: Everyone at this office is professional and friendly and they make you feel welcome. I highly recommend this dentist and staff.  Dr. Nick is awesome and his assistant Melissa was so kind  and caring.

reviews.author: Tiffany Cornelius
reviews.text: Dr. Villafria & the entire team are the best there are, plain & simple. I used to have so much fear of going to the dentist, and everything is thoroughly explained beforehand, done gently & thoroughly, and with so much care. I couldn't imagine going anywhere else now.

reviews.author: Cat
reviews.text: Super friendly and caring. They listen and understand your needs. I have had a hard time finding a dentist I was comfortable with. I will be staying with Tampa Dental.

reviews.author: robert buggica
reviews.text: They are all so very friendly there. Brittany is still amazing. She was very gentle and so easy to talk to. She kept asking me if something was sensitive or hurt if she poked me while cleaning my teeth. She is so kind. I live in St. Petersburg now, but as long as she's there I'll continue to be a patient.

reviews.author: Jonathan Viera
reviews.text: Dr. Christina was amazing… she cared for my pain and filled in my tooth perfectly. She made sure I was not feeling no pain before she worked on the tooth. She was very nice from the start and very professional.

reviews.author: Alex Bradley
reviews.text: Even though my dental hygienist knew her stuff and articulated it to me very well, she had no social skills at all.  I've already asked for a different one for my next visit. Maybe her next patient,  she'll introduce herself with her name and ask me mine....

reviews.author: Bill Cagle
reviews.text: Always a great experience. Makes you feel you are being very well taken care of and secure in they know what they are doing.

reviews.author: David Roake
reviews.text: 10/10 everyone there is great.

reviews.author: Peter Tomasello
reviews.text: Every appointment I have had with Tampa Dental went extremely well including my appointment yesterday.  A staff that has been very professional, knowledgeable and efficient.  I highly recommend Tampa Dental if you're looking for quality dental work.

reviews.author: Virginia C
reviews.text: Everyone is super expert and personable in their job.
